To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fuzzy control systems are more robust than neural control systems when their FAM rules are removed or replaced with destructive rules.
fuzzy systems are less robust than neural systems but are more robust than the underlying fuzzy associative memory rules.

fuzzy and neural control systems for truck and trailer backing are robust to the removal of FAM rules, and that fuzzy and neural systems can be converted into FAM rule systems by DCL or product space clustering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of adaptive control algorithms for backing up a trailer with a truck.
the design and implementation of a fuzzy system for controlling a vehicle.
developing fuzzy systems for control of dynamic systems, and with the use of these fuzzy systems for the adaptive generation of control rules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fuzzy systems were robust and the neural systems were adaptive.
the DCL and product space clustering systems are the best of the systems tested in this thesis for generating FAM rules for backing up a vehicle.
the fuzzy systems were the most robust and efficient, the neural systems required the least amount of training data, and the adaptive systems were the fastest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

adaptive fuzzy control systems can be trained to perform as well or better than neural control systems, and that they can be trained to recover their original performance if the training data are corrupted.
adaptive fuzzy systems have the potential to perform well in the truck backing up problem.
fuzzy and neural systems are robust to random rule removal, but that fuzzy systems are more robust than neural systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fuzzy systems are robust to random removal of FAM rules, but they are susceptible to removal of their key FAM equilibriating rules.
the FAM rules of a well-trained fuzzy control system can be used for the design of an adaptive fuzzy system.
the DCL algorithm is a powerful tool to adaptively generate fuzzy control rules for complex nonlinear systems.
